metadata.title: My Wife Stopped Blinking at 3AM
metadata.subtitle: She is sitting right beside me on the couch—so who is texting me from our locked bedroom?

nodes.text: 2:58 AM · Hannah sits beside you staring at the black TV screen. She hasn’t blinked in 4 minutes. Her phone sits face-down on the table—yet your phone buzzes with a text from her.
{{player_name}} DON’T MOVE. Do not let her see you reading this. I am locked in the upstairs bedroom.
Hannah? You’re sitting two feet away from me right now. Stop joking.

nodes.transcript: [sobbing softly] "I never made it downstairs, {{player_name}}! Whatever came back from the cabin with you doesn’t know how to blink!"

nodes.text: Ask the thing on the couch what we named our golden retriever.

nodes.prompt: The woman beside you slowly turns her neck 90 degrees:

options.label: Ask her our old dog’s name casually
options.player_reply_text: Hey honey, what was our old dog’s name again?

options.label: Text Dr. Cole about her cabin ER visit
options.player_reply_text: Dr. Cole, did Hannah actually get discharged from Pine Ridge ER tonight?

nodes.text: Dr. Cole texts back urgently: "{{player_name}}, Hannah was never discharged—she vanished from triage 3 hours ago!"
No! {{player_name}}, Hannah never left Pine Ridge ER—her wristband was found cut in the parking lot at midnight!
The woman on the couch smiles too wide—teeth clicking like dry porcelain—and whispers: "Who are you texting?"
Run to the kitchen and grab the spare brass key! Don’t break eye contact with her or she’ll lunge!
I’m backing toward the stairs... she didn’t follow me. She’s just laughing in the dark.

nodes.headline: Locked Behind the Bedroom Door
nodes.teaser_text: Next: You reach the upstairs door—and hear two voices pleading from inside.

nodes.text: 3:05 AM · The upstairs hallway is pitch-black. Only the blue glow of your phone lights the floorboards.
I can hear your footsteps outside! Slide your phone camera under the gap so I know it’s really you!
I’m right here, Hannah! Unlock the deadbolt—we’re climbing out the balcony!

nodes.transcript: [urgent, siren in background] "{{player_name}}, police just found Hannah’s coat in the woods! Nobody drove home from the cabin—who is in your house?!"

nodes.text: Don’t listen to Dr. Cole. He doesn’t know about the attic.

nodes.prompt: Fingernails tap impatiently on the inside of the bedroom door:

options.label: Ask what happened at the mountain cabin
options.player_reply_text: Tell me what really happened at Pine Ridge before I turn this key!

options.label: Check the hallway motion camera first
options.player_reply_text: Hold on, I’m checking the upstairs hallway security feed.

nodes.text: Something followed us into the car! I hid in the trunk until we reached the garage, then ran upstairs!
Don’t look at the camera—it’s standing right behind you in the corridor!!
The bedroom lock clicks open by itself. Inside, the room is empty—except the attic ladder hangs down.
Wait—the police dispatcher says your car has been parked in your garage for 4 DAYS, {{player_name}}!
That’s impossible... I just drove back from the mountains tonight... didn’t I?

nodes.headline: Four Missing Days
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The corridor shadow cam shows who actually walked upstairs.

nodes.text: 3:11 AM · Your smart-home app pings a motion alert from the corridor directly behind you.
Climb up to the attic, {{player_name}}. It can’t climb the wooden rungs—hurry!
Wait. If you’re in the attic, why is my hallway cam showing someone standing 3 meters behind me?

nodes.transcript: [whispering, floorboards creaking overhead] "Because the one from the couch finally stood up! Look at the photo!"

nodes.text: It wears my face, but it only copies memories stored in your cloud backup.

nodes.caption: Corridor cam 03:11 — a motionless figure standing at the far end of the upstairs hallway.

nodes.prompt: The shadow takes one silent glide toward you:

options.label: Climb into the attic and pull the ladder
options.player_reply_text: I’m climbing up now—pull the ladder behind me!

options.label: Throw your phone flashlight at the shadow
options.player_reply_text: I’m flashing the beam straight at its face!

nodes.text: Dr. Cole texts: "Do NOT go into the attic, {{player_name}}! Police found blood stains on your attic hatch last Tuesday!"
Dr. Cole texts: "Its eyes didn’t reflect the light because it’s not alive—GET OUT OF THE HOUSE!"
You slam the bedroom door and wedge a chair beneath the knob. Something presses softly against the wood—without breathing.
Why did you stop halfway up the ladder, {{player_name}}? Don’t you remember what we hid up here?
What did we hide? Hannah... why is your voice echoing from INSIDE the attic walls?

nodes.headline: The Cloud Backup Rehearsal
nodes.teaser_text: Next: Your phone’s cloud sync log reveals a terrifying 4-day loop.

nodes.text: 3:18 AM · A notification pops up on your phone: "Cloud Memory Backup — 99% Restored. 4,210 Voice Clips Indexed."
{{player_name}}, officers are 4 minutes out. Do NOT trust any voice note—someone downloaded all of Hannah’s old voicemails!
Downloaded them? Wait... who had my cloud password besides Hannah?
Listen to the pitch splice—it’s stitching her old voice notes together in real time.

nodes.prompt: Your attic phone keeps ringing while the hallway stays dead silent:

options.label: Check the bedroom nightstand drawer
options.player_reply_text: I’m checking her nightstand—her passport and purse are still here!

options.label: Inspect the deleted cloud videos
options.player_reply_text: There’s a deleted video from 4 days ago in the cloud trash...

nodes.text: If her purse never left the house, then she NEVER went to the mountain cabin alone!
Play it! That video shows the exact moment the mimic stepped out of the fireplace!
The chair wedged against the bedroom door scrapes 3 inches backward. Something heavy leans against the outside.
Wait—the patrol sergeant just pulled your marriage records! {{player_name}}, Hannah passed away 6 months ago!
Stop lying to me!! I ate dinner with her tonight! Her wedding ring is right here on the dresser!

nodes.headline: Six Months Gone
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The scratch inside the wedding ring breaks the entire illusion.

nodes.text: 3:25 AM · Every bulb in the bedroom dims to a sickly amber. The attic hatch creaks open by itself.
Don’t listen to Dr. Cole, {{player_name}}. Remember why you asked me to stay? You hated sleeping in an empty house.
I didn’t ask a monster to wear my wife’s face! Stay back!

nodes.transcript: [soft, eerie hum] "Then why did you upload 4,000 of her voice notes into the basement server, {{player_name}}?"

nodes.text: You invited me in on the night of the funeral.

nodes.prompt: Blue and red police lights flash across the bedroom curtains:

options.label: Run for the front stairs now
options.player_reply_text: The police are here—I’m making a break for the stairs!

options.label: Grab the wedding ring off the dresser
options.player_reply_text: I’m grabbing her ring first—I need to see the engraving!

nodes.text: Don’t open the front door! If they see me, they’ll realize I never blink!
Drop that ring! That’s the only real piece of her left in this house!
You clutch the cold gold band in your palm. Suddenly the attic voice falls completely silent.
We’re at your front door, {{player_name}}! Drop the curtain and let the officers in—wait, who is standing in the upstairs window?!
I’m NOT at the window... I’m standing in the doorway...

nodes.headline: The Face in the Window
nodes.teaser_text: Next: The wedding ring engraving reveals the truth about the night she died.

nodes.text: 3:30 AM · You hold the wedding ring under your phone flashlight. Deep, frantic scratches cover the inner band.
{{player_name}}, the officers forced the front lock! Stay where you are—they’re sweeping the first floor!
Wait... there’s a message scratched inside her ring. It says "NOT DEAD — ATTIC WALL".

nodes.transcript: [raw, human, gasping for air] "Don’t let the thing downstairs fool the police! It took my place in the coffin—I’ve been hiding behind the attic insulation!"

nodes.text: If you tell them, I’ll wear YOUR face next.

nodes.caption: Hannah’s wedding ring left beside the bed — tiny fresh scratches etched along the inner gold band.

nodes.prompt: Heavy boots climb the staircase toward you:

options.label: Scream for the police to search the attic
options.player_reply_text: OFFICERS! UP HERE! CHECK BEHIND THE ATTIC WALL!

options.label: Rip open the attic insulation yourself
options.player_reply_text: Hold on Hannah, I’m tearing the insulation open right now!

nodes.text: Officers just reached the second floor! Wait—the couch downstairs is completely empty, only a pile of cold ash!
They hear you! Officers are right behind you with crowbars—don’t look back at the hallway!
Two officers pry open the false plywood panel in the attic. Behind it sits a shivering, bruised woman—blinking furiously in the flashlight beam.
She has a pulse! It’s the real Hannah—she’s dehydrated and hypothermic, we’re loading her into the ambulance now!
Thank God... wait. If the real Hannah was behind that wall, then where did the thing from the couch go?!

nodes.headline: Gone Into the Rain
nodes.teaser_text: Finale next: One final text arrives from the ambulance parking lot.

nodes.text: 3:42 AM · You sit in the back of the ambulance holding Hannah’s freezing hand as sirens cut through the rain.
{{player_name}}, I’m in the front cab with the driver. Keep talking to Hannah so she stays awake until we hit the ER.
She’s quiet... she’s just staring at the ambulance ceiling light.

nodes.transcript: [static from your coat pocket—Hannah’s REAL phone] "{{player_name}}!! I’m still on the stretcher at the house!! Who did you get in the ambulance with?!"

nodes.text: She hasn’t blinked since the doors shut.

nodes.prompt: The woman on the stretcher slowly turns her head toward you:

options.label: Bang on the cab glass for Dr. Cole
options.player_reply_text: DR. COLE! STOP THE AMBULANCE RIGHT NOW!

options.label: Pull the emergency rear-door handle
options.player_reply_text: I’m pulling the emergency release—stay away from me!

nodes.text: The driver slams the brakes! The rear doors fly open—and police cruisers box the ambulance in from behind!
You leap onto the wet asphalt as the police cruiser’s floodlights blind the ambulance bay—inside, the stretcher is completely empty!
Ten seconds later, the second ambulance pulls up. The real Hannah leans out, tears streaming—blinking rapidly as she calls your name.
I’m right here, {{player_name}}. Whatever that thing was, it dropped your spare phone on the stretcher and vanished into the trees.
Wait... my screen just lit up with a new message from an unknown number: "Next time, I’ll remember to blink."

nodes.headline: Next Time, It Will Blink
nodes.teaser_text: Act 2 begins: The ambulance takes a sharp turn away from the hospital—and real Hannah calls from your driveway.

nodes.text: 03:46 AM · Rain lashes the ambulance windows. Your map app shows the van turning away from St. Jude ER toward the riverfront tunnels.
Stop looking at your phone, {{player_name}}. The doctor said bright screens delay my recovery.

nodes.transcript: [sirens wailing behind her] "Jump out at the next intersection! The real paramedics just arrived—that van has no license plate!"

nodes.prompt: The van slows for a flooded crosswalk. The thing on the stretcher reaches for your wrist:

options.label: Yank the rear latch & roll out
options.player_reply_text: Stay away from me!

options.label: Snatch its ER wristband before jumping
options.player_reply_text: I am taking proof of what you are.

nodes.text: You kick the rear handle open and tumble into the freezing puddle as the van speeds away into the fog.
You rip the plastic wristband off its ice-cold arm—it reads "SUBJECT 07-B · WARD 4B"—before diving onto the wet asphalt.
I made it out! Hannah, where are the real paramedics taking you?
{{player_name}}, I am at St. Jude ER right now. I was NEVER in that ambulance with you.

nodes.headline: The Stolen Badge
nodes.teaser_text: If Dr. Cole never left the ER, who was driving the fake ambulance—and where did it just park?

nodes.text: 04:08 AM · Shivering in the back of a police cruiser heading to St. Jude ER, you open the tracking ping from the phone you dropped inside the fake van.

nodes.caption: GPS trace 04:05 — the fake ambulance stopped at an unmarked riverfront clinic, alongside 14 other 3AM pings across town.

nodes.text: Wait... I recognize that warehouse address. The hospital decommissioned that cryo-annex two years ago.
Someone used my badge number to unlock the morgue annex at 2:40 AM.

nodes.prompt: You saw Dr. Cole unsent that message before it vanished:

options.label: Ask him directly about his stolen badge
options.player_reply_text: Doc, why did you unsend that? Who has your ID?

options.label: Screenshot the GPS map & send to Hannah
options.player_reply_text: Keep this map safe—14 other families are marked.

nodes.text: I reported my spare keycard lost last month! Whoever took it cloned my voice and credentials.
Oh God... the red dot three streets over is Sarah’s house. She told me yesterday her husband stopped sleeping!
This isn’t just about us. There are fourteen mimics active in our neighborhood tonight.
Get to Room 302 right now, {{player_name}}. I finally remember where I saw that clinic before.

nodes.headline: The Fourteen Mirrors
nodes.teaser_text: Hannah remembers the 4-day sleep study after her crash—and why the mimic knew every word of your vows.

nodes.text: 04:28 AM · Room 302, St. Jude ER. Hannah sits under bright fluorescent lights, blinking tearfully as she grips your warm fingers.
Six months ago after my fender-bender, a private neuro-clinic offered me a free 4-day sleep trial for my migraines.
Wait—the same four missing days from our cloud backup?!

nodes.transcript: [voice trembling] "They made me read our old texts out loud under a blue scanner—they told me it was a memory-calibration test!"

nodes.prompt: A cold realization hits you about the clinic’s intake forms:

options.label: Check who signed Hannah’s referral
options.player_reply_text: Who referred you to that clinic, Hannah?

options.label: Check if YOUR name is on their visitor log
options.player_reply_text: Wait—did I pick you up from that clinic?

nodes.text: The referral had St. Jude’s stamp on it. I thought Dr. Cole’s department sent it!
You waited in their lounge for two hours—and they offered you a "free stress scan" while you waited...
I just pulled the hospital archive. I never signed a referral for Hannah—someone forged the entire transfer packet.
Worse: look at the date stamped on the bottom of her consent form.

nodes.headline: Signed Before The Crash
nodes.teaser_text: The forged consent form is dated four days BEFORE Hannah’s car crash even happened.

nodes.text: 04:42 AM · Dr. Cole slides a high-res scan from the hospital archive directly into your chat.

nodes.caption: Intake Form #07-B — signed four days BEFORE Hannah’s crash, listing "Neural Mirroring & Replacement Pilot."

nodes.text: They staged her car crash just to get her inside that lab?!
And look at the witness line—every single one of the 14 addresses on your GPS map had a "minor accident" this year.

nodes.prompt: The ER hallway lights suddenly buzz and dim to half power:

options.label: Lock Room 302 from the inside
options.player_reply_text: Bar the door—they tracked our phones here!

options.label: Forward the forged file to the police
options.player_reply_text: Sending everything to the precinct right now.

nodes.text: You click the heavy deadbolt shut just as slow, wet footsteps pause right outside Room 302’s frosted glass.
Upload 100% sent to Police Cyber Unit—one second before the hospital’s cellular signal jams to zero bars.
Do not turn around, {{player_name}}. Someone is standing behind the curtain.
Hannah, you are sitting right in front of me—why did your phone just vibrate with my own caller ID?!

nodes.headline: Calling From Inside The Ward
nodes.teaser_text: Your phone rings with YOUR OWN NAME on the caller screen—and the voice on the line knows what you’re wearing.

nodes.text: 04:50 AM · The hospital corridor goes dead silent. Your screen lights up with an impossible caller ID.

nodes.transcript: [recording from the hallway intercom—it’s YOUR exact voice] "Why did you leave Hannah in the ambulance? Open Room 302. I forgot my keys."

nodes.text: That’s your voice... word for word, breath for breath. They didn’t just scan me at that clinic!

nodes.prompt: Knuckles tap rhythmically against the glass door of Room 302:

options.label: Yell that the police are on their way
options.player_reply_text: Stay out! Police are already downstairs!

options.label: Pull the red fire-alarm lever inside
options.player_reply_text: Let’s see how mimics handle bright lights and alarms!

nodes.text: The tapping stops instantly. A flat, unblinking smile presses against the frosted glass—wearing YOUR face—then retreats down the hall.
Strobe lights flash and sprinklers hiss! Security guards flood the third floor as the figure wearing your face sprints for the stairwell.
Security just sent me the third-floor CCTV still from two minutes ago. Brace yourself.
Send it. If there’s another me out there, I need to see where it went.

nodes.headline: Corridor Camera 04:53
nodes.teaser_text: The hospital CCTV shows two identical silhouettes outside the stairwell—heading straight for the sub-basement.

nodes.text: 05:02 AM · The fire alarm cuts out, leaving the third floor smelling of ozone and wet concrete. Dr. Cole forwards the CCTV capture.

nodes.caption: Stairwell CCTV 04:53 — two motionless figures standing side by side at the sub-basement hatch, waiting for the lift.

nodes.text: Wait... why are there TWO of them? One has your coat, and the other is wearing my blue hospital gown!
They went down to the old steam tunnel connecting St. Jude directly to the riverfront cryo-annex!

nodes.prompt: Dr. Cole says the tunnel seal locks automatically at 05:30:

options.label: Follow the tunnel with Hannah right now
options.player_reply_text: We end this tonight before they escape.

options.label: Grab Dr. Cole’s master override key first
options.player_reply_text: Toss me the master key—we’re shutting down the lab.

nodes.text: You wedge a steel fire extinguisher in the tunnel door so it can’t lock behind you and descend into the humming dark.
Catch! The brass key opens the lab’s thermal purge panel—if you raise the room above 38°C, the mimics shut down.

nodes.transcript: [echoing over radio] "Warning! The lab server just started a countdown called SYNC 100%. You have twenty minutes!"

nodes.text: What happens when Sync hits 100%?!

nodes.headline: The Sync 100% Rule
nodes.teaser_text: Once a mimic reaches 100% sync and blinks for the first time, the biological original never wakes up again.

nodes.text: 05:14 AM · Frost coats the steel pipes at the end of the steam tunnel. Cold blue light leaks under a heavy vault door labeled WARD 4B.
I decrypted the protocol! The mimics can’t blink because their neural link is still tethered to the original sleepers inside Ward 4B.
Wait... if the originals are sleeping inside Ward 4B, then how is Hannah standing right next to me?
Because I never left the cryo-chamber six months ago.

nodes.prompt: You glance sideways at Hannah walking beside you in the frost:

options.label: Check if her breath fogs the cold air
options.player_reply_text: Hannah... why isn’t your breath steaming?

options.label: Grab her hand to feel her pulse
options.player_reply_text: Your wrist is freezing—where is your pulse?!

nodes.text: Your own breath billows in thick white clouds—while hers leaves the icy air completely clear and still.
Her skin feels warm on the surface—a clever upgrade—until you press her wrist artery and feel ZERO heartbeat.
Open the vault door, {{player_name}}. You wanted to see the truth behind the glass.
You led me straight down here on purpose...

nodes.headline: Act 3 · Glass Tank 07
nodes.teaser_text: Fourteen glass chambers line the frozen corridor—and inside Tank 07 lies the real, shivering Hannah.

nodes.text: 05:21 AM · The vault door groans open into a cathedral of frosted glass pods. Every pod holds a sleeping neighbor from your GPS map.

nodes.caption: Ward 4B main aisle — a tall silhouette standing between Tank 07 and the thermal control console.

nodes.text: Dr. Cole, I found them! Fourteen pods—and Hannah is inside Tank 07! Her heart monitor is blinking weakly!
Version One in the ambulance was clumsy. I was built to blink when you watched, cry when you cried—just to bring you here.

nodes.prompt: Version Two blocks the path to Tank 07 while the Sync timer hits 94%:

options.label: Sprint past her toward Tank 07
options.player_reply_text: Get out of my way—I’m taking my wife home!

options.label: Ask why she wears the ring on the wrong hand
options.player_reply_text: You copied her face, not her left hand.

nodes.text: You shoulder past her icy grip and slam your palms against Tank 07’s frost—inside, real Hannah’s eyes flutter open!
Mirror-image scan error... how irritating. You always noticed the tiniest scratches, didn’t you?
Don’t break the glass yet! If you shatter the seal before disconnecting the neural feed, the shock will stop her heart!
Wait—the intercom panel on Tank 07 is lighting up! She’s pressing the emergency talk button from inside!

nodes.headline: The Ring Doesn’t Lie
nodes.teaser_text: Real Hannah’s voice crackles through Tank 07’s intercom—revealing the one thing Version Two couldn’t copy.

nodes.text: 05:27 AM · Sync Timer: 96%. Version Two locks the vault door from the control desk while a second shadow—wearing YOUR coat—steps out behind her.
Don’t fight it, {{player_name}}. Once your copy finishes syncing, we’ll both live in your house—young, tireless, never sick again.
You’re not human. You don’t even know what love feels like—you only repeat what you scraped off our phones!

nodes.transcript: [urgent whisper] "I hacked the room’s ventilation! Flip the red breaker on the north wall—heat breaks the neural tether safely!"

nodes.prompt: Your mimic steps toward you, mimicking your exact posture:

options.label: Hurl a steel chair at the server rack
options.player_reply_text: Let’s see your precious server survive this!

options.label: Answer the intercom call from Tank 07
options.player_reply_text: Hang on, Hannah—I hear you!

nodes.text: Sparks erupt across the main console! Both mimics stagger backward, their synchronized smiles glitching into frozen terror.
You slam the intercom button on Tank 07—flooding the chamber with real Hannah’s voice, causing Version Two to clutch her temples in agony.
They’re stunned! Hannah, talk to me—the intercom line is patching straight to my phone!
Pick it up! She knows the manual release code etched inside the pod!

nodes.headline: The Real Voice Inside
nodes.teaser_text: After six months trapped in ice, real Hannah calls you directly from Tank 07 with the key to destroy the lab.

nodes.text: 05:31 AM · Tank 07’s emergency bridge dials your phone as the overhead alarms flash crimson.

nodes.transcript: [gasping, tears in her voice] "{{player_name}}! The release code is our wedding date—0914! Hit thermal purge first or all fourteen pods lock forever!"

nodes.text: I’m right here, sweetheart! I’m hitting the thermal purge right now!

nodes.prompt: Your mimic lunges for the red thermal breaker to stop you:

options.label: Slide under its arm & pull the breaker
options.player_reply_text: Time to thaw this place out!

options.label: Enter 0914 to unlock all 14 pods at once
options.player_reply_text: Nobody gets left behind tonight!

nodes.text: You slam the red lever down! Scorching steam blasts from the ceiling vents, flooding the cold corridor in blinding white heat.
ALL 14 CHAMBERS UNLOCKED! Hydraulic latches pop down the entire aisle as scorching steam pours in to fry the mimic links.
Room temp just hit 39°C! The Sync countdown collapsed to 0%—the mimics are shutting down!
Version Two just collapsed—and Tank 07’s glass lid is sliding open!

nodes.headline: Manual Purge Complete
nodes.teaser_text: The mimics freeze in the 39°C heat, but the clinic’s self-destruct lockdown starts ticking down from two minutes.

nodes.text: 05:36 AM · You catch real Hannah as she tumbles out of Tank 07—shivering, sobbing, blinking rapidly, her pulse hammering against your chest.
You really found me... I could hear your voice through the glass every time that thing practiced smiling.
Police tactical units just breached the riverfront entrance! Follow the green exit strips up the service stairs—now!
Wait—the body of my mimic isn’t on the floor anymore.

nodes.prompt: Smoke thickens near the stairwell as other rescued neighbors stumble out:

options.label: Carry Hannah up the stairs first
options.player_reply_text: Hold onto my neck—we’re getting out!

options.label: Help Sarah & neighbors reach the exit too
options.player_reply_text: Grab my shoulder, everyone up the stairs!

nodes.text: You lift Hannah into your arms and charge up three flights of steel steps as flashlights and sirens sweep down to meet you.
You guide four dazed neighbors alongside Hannah straight into the arms of the rescue team—not a single soul left behind.
I see you coming out the service doors! Paramedics have warm blankets ready for Hannah.
Dr. Cole—tell the police to check the riverfront road. One mimic didn’t collapse in the steam.

nodes.headline: Out Into The Rain
nodes.teaser_text: All fourteen victims are rescued as dawn breaks—but police only recovered thirteen mimic bodies from Ward 4B.

nodes.text: 06:30 AM · Soft gray dawn breaks over St. Jude Hospital. Rain drips off the eaves while police tape seals the riverfront warehouse.
Good news first: Hannah’s vitals are 100% normal, and the clinic’s directors were just arrested at the airport.
Thank you for never giving up on me, {{player_name}}. Even when I couldn’t tell you the truth.

nodes.transcript: [lowering his voice] "One strange detail, though—forensics counted thirteen inactive mimics downstairs. The fourteenth pod was empty before the purge."

nodes.prompt: Hannah yawns sleepily in the warm hospital bed and reaches for your hand:

options.label: Kiss her forehead & promise it’s over
options.player_reply_text: Sleep now, Hannah. You’re finally safe.

options.label: Check the wedding ring on her left hand
options.player_reply_text: Left hand, tiny scratch inside—100% my wife.

nodes.text: Stay right here until I wake up, okay? Don’t leave the room.
[soft laugh] You really checked the scratch again. I love you, you stubborn detective.
As Hannah drifts into a deep, peaceful sleep, you step over to the sunlit window to stretch your stiff shoulders.
Hey {{player_name}}, quick check—whose name was on that fourteenth empty pod?

nodes.headline: The Empty Fourteenth Pod
nodes.teaser_text: Morning sunlight floods the hospital glass—and your own reflection reveals the final, unforgettable twist.

nodes.text: 07:15 AM · Golden morning sunlight pours across the hospital room. Birds chirp outside, and the rain is completely gone.
Police just read me the brass tag from Pod 14. {{player_name}}... it has YOUR name on it. Dated six months ago.
Wait... that’s impossible. I saved Hannah. I fought the mimic in the steam...
When you sat in the waiting room six months ago, you never walked back out.

nodes.prompt: You stare into the sunlit window glass at your own reflection:

options.label: Try to blink right now
options.player_reply_text: Come on... blink. Why can’t I blink?

options.label: Check your smartwatch heart-rate screen
options.player_reply_text: Wait—why has my watch been stuck on 36.8°C?

nodes.text: You stare at the bright sun for sixty full seconds. Your eyes don’t water. Your eyelids don’t even twitch—until you force them shut.
Your watch displays a tiny green status line you never noticed before: "MODEL 14 · EMPATHY OVERRIDE ACTIVE · PROTECT SUBJECT 07."
{{player_name}}? Come back to bed, my love. You’re staring at the window without blinking again.
I’m coming, Hannah. I’ll protect you—no matter what I really am.

nodes.headline: Series Finale · Model 14
nodes.teaser_text: You saved the real Hannah from the ice—only to realize the most terrifying secret of all: you were the one mimic who learned how to love.
